headline: South Asia: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

At 88, Merle Stern has little interest in measuring her life by the accolades she has racked up. For the retired justice of the peace, the greater reward has been the opportunity to help people through their difficulties, restore relationships, and ensure that the needs of the vulnerable are not overlooked.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting.
Developments in the Gulf region amid the US-Israeli war on Iran came under discussion as the R4 foreign ministers — Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — met with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. The R4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO.
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed the ratification processes for the Makkah defence pact while Turkiye was in the process of doing so, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR.

- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, Jerusalem Post, 9 hours ago: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events.
An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections. An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron. The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers.

It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed. Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.

The military said residents in areas where its forces are operating would be allowed to leave through three designated exit points.
